subject: CloudRise Private Offer + co-sell: integration gaps & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CloudRise Private Offer + co-sell: integration gaps & next steps

Team —

Quick summary: CloudRise (prospect) wants to list on AWS and run a PrivateOffer flow for an initial pilot with a healthcare customer. They also want to enable co-sell with AWS for later stages. I attached the integration brief they sent last week.

Open questions we need to cover before I loop in their procurement:
- SKU mapping / metering: does our metering shim support their usage pattern (short-lived inference jobs + volume-tier discounts)?
- PrivateOffer creation: do we need any special seller onboarding on our side (AOR, SSA) to accept a PrivateOffer?
- Co-sell enablement: what metadata do we need in the listing to be co-sell eligible (tags, pricing commitments)?
- Timeline: CloudRise wants a 3-week turnaround for pilot procurement. Is that realistic?

Olga — can you confirm the metering capabilities and any changes required? Vivek — can you call out the sales ops/clould-marketplace steps (onboarding, partner tax/agreements)?

Next steps: I’ll draft the outreach to their procurement when we have the answers.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: cloudrise_integration_brief.pdf
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CloudRise Private Offer + co-sell: integration gaps & next steps

Ben / Vivek —

Thanks — quick answers below and I attached a working metering map. High level:

- Metering shim: supports short-lived job-based metering. We expose a token-based usage meter and can map job types to SKUs. The main limitation is per-job aggregated billing latency (we flush aggregates every 6 hours). If CloudRise needs near-real-time reconciliation, we’ll need to add a small webhook to push aggregates.

- Volume tiers: supported at the SKU level; we can configure thresholds. The engineering effort to add a new tiered SKU for a partner is ~3 days (including QA).

- PrivateOffer / seller onboarding: no infra changes required for the runtime. Marketplace-side we need the seller (CloudRise) to complete the AWS seller onboarding and provide their AWS account ID so we can create the PrivateOffer. We also need to confirm who signs the AWS-side partner agreement.

- Co-sell tags: listing needs publisher contact, SKU-level pricing, and a co-sell contact alias. AWS requires an overwrite-able commitment field in the offer metadata (we can populate this at listing time).

I attached: metering-mapping.xlsx (prototype SKU <> job-type map).

Happy to jump on a short call with CloudRise SEs to walk the mapping.

—Olga
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: metering-mapping.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@cloudrise.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + quick asks for CloudRise marketplace & PrivateOffer flow

Hi Sasha —

Nice to meet you (via email). We’ve been working internally on the marketplace listing path and to make the PrivateOffer + co-sell handoff smooth. Olga (cc’d) is our partner integrations lead and will handle the metering mapping.

Can you confirm for procurement:
1) Who at CloudRise will create/authorize the AWS PrivateOffer (name + email + AWS account ID)?
2) Do you have standard PO terms or a procurement checklist we should expect?
3) Any timeline constraints for the pilot (they mentioned a 3-week target)?

Also attaching our public-facing catalog requirements so you can see the metadata we will need on the listing. If you can share your procurement doc/terms that would speed things up.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min alignment call this week with your SE + procurement.

Best,
Ben
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_catalog_requirements.pdf
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@cloudrise.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
Cc: procurement@cloudrise.com
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + quick asks for CloudRise marketplace & PrivateOffer flow

Ben —

Thanks for the note. Quick answers and a couple of asks: we’ve attached our procurement terms (cloudrise_po_terms.pdf).

1) PrivateOffer owner: procurement@cloudrise.com will create the offer but needs the seller contact and the pricing SKU mapping from Redwood. We can share the AWS account ID once seller onboarding is confirmed.

2) Procurement terms: attached. We typically require a 45-day net payment term for pilots unless a customer makes an exception; is Redwood able to accept shorter terms for pilot customers?

3) Timeline: 3 weeks is tight but doable if we lock the SKU mapping and seller onboarding within 5 business days.

Questions from our finance team:
- How are refunds/credits handled if a pilot underutilizes committed spend?
- Is there a standard invoice flow (PO -> invoice -> payment) and will it be Redwood invoicing CloudRise or the end customer?

We’d like a short technical sync with Olga to validate the metering map and confirm if any webhook changes are required. Can you propose 2 times?

Best,
Sasha Ivanov
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudRise

Attachment: cloudrise_po_terms.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Sasha Ivanov <sasha@cloudrise.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.example>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + quick asks for CloudRise marketplace & PrivateOffer flow

Sasha —

Thanks, got the terms. Quick responses inline and a proposed MAP below.

On payment terms / invoicing:
- Refunds/credits: we can support consumption reconciliation and issue credits for demonstrable over-commitment. Our standard approach is to invoice based on metered usage per agreed SKU mapping; for pilot commitments we can issue pro-rated credits if utilization falls below the contracted threshold. We’ll document the reconciliation cadence in the MAP.
- Invoice flow: Redwood will invoice CloudRise (as the seller) only when charges flow through Redwood’s metering shim and the agreed billing account. For PrivateOffer setups where Redwood is the listed publisher but CloudRise is the seller, we’ll mirror the usual marketplace flow — CloudRise will be the billing entity to the end customer; Redwood will share metered usage for reconciliation. We can add a short legal addendum if needed.

Proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — timeline (3 weeks target):
Week 1:
- Day 1–3: Seller onboarding + exchange of AWS account IDs; procurement confirms PO terms (CloudRise).
- Day 4–7: Olga + CloudRise SE validate metering-mapping.xlsx; finalize SKU mapping and webhook plan.
Week 2:
- Day 8–12: Create PrivateOffer draft in AWS; Redwood validates listing metadata and co-sell tags.
- Day 13–14: Internal approvals (legal & finance) and DocuSign routing.
Week 3:
- Day 15–21: Pilot goes live; daily reconciliation for first 72 hours, then 6-hour aggregate flush.

Olga — can you confirm: if we need a webhook, we estimate ~3 days of engineering effort. If CloudRise can accept the 6-hour aggregate flush for the pilot, that reduces lift.

Sasha — propose 30-min sync: Tue 06/09 at 10:00AM PT or Wed 06/10 at 2:00PM PT?

Links: HubSpot: https://hubspot.example/contacts/CR-001234; DocuSign (placeholder): https://www.docusign.com/Sign/placeholder-link

Thanks,
Ben

- Metering: SEs validated the metering-mapping.xlsx for the job types we expect. We can accept the 6-hour aggregate flush for the pilot. For longer-term production we’ll want the webhook; put that as a Q3 engineering ticket.

We attached a short agenda for a sales-engineering enablement call (sales_enablement_agenda.docx). Can we lock Tue 06/09 at 10:00AM PT for the sync?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving quickly.

Best,
Sasha Ivanov
Head of Platform Partnerships
CloudRise
